result.summary: Conditional proposal: narrow first-search context with a small, ranked set and an explicit continuation path.
alternatives: Progressive result batches
A concise relevance-ranked summary with continuation
risks: Abandonment may have causes other than result volume; P3 leaves that unexplained.
result.nextAction: Product owner should trial a bounded first batch and revision-safe continuation on the 12-session sample, then check abandonment and missing-result reports.
uncertainties: No interview explains why four users abandoned.

result.summary: Conditional proposal: improve request completeness and discoverability without forcing replies or waking volunteers.
alternatives: A completeness prompt for new questions
A filter for unanswered, reproducible questions
risks: Better formatting may not create volunteer capacity; P3 is unmeasured.
result.nextAction: Community owner should trial an unanswered/reproducible view and a request template, then check reply rate and volunteer availability without automatic waking.

Filter open questions with no reply after two days; P1

result.summary: Conditional proposal: return a bounded first page and require revision-safe continuation so the last-row exception remains reachable.
alternatives: Paged results with continuation
A compact table summary plus linked full rows
risks: Clients that do not continue may miss detail; silent truncation would hide the critical exception.
result.nextAction: API owner should specify a bounded page with a continuation token tied to the current revision, then verify that the last-row exception is returned on continuation.
uncertainties: Client continuation behavior and the exact page split are not established.

alternatives.label: Compact summary with linked full rows

structured.reason: Prefer paged continuation because D2 requires preserving a critical exception and D3 provides a safe access mechanism; D1 supplies the current response bound.
uncertainty: The client may stop after page one; exact page size is unmeasured.
minority: A compact summary could reduce first-response size if every exception remains directly reachable.

reviewConditions: Verify every row, including the last-row exception, is reachable through revision-safe continuation
Check that no permission change or silent omission occurs
structured.revisit: Revisit after a bounded client compatibility check and exception-retrieval verification.

result.summary: Conditional proposal: use targeted refresh for changed paths and a full scan at controlled reconciliation points, with freshness labels.
alternatives: Targeted event refresh plus periodic reconciliation
Full scan every minute
risks: Dropped events can leave stale entries between reconciliations; cold-start cost is unknown.
result.nextAction: Index owner should run a bounded reconciliation trial and measure cold-start timing before selecting an interval; stale source content must remain marked stale.
uncertainties: Cold-start timings and an acceptable reconciliation interval are unknown.

alternatives.label: Targeted refresh plus periodic full reconciliation

structured.reason: Prefer the implemented targeted refresh with explicit reconciliation because D1 shows events can be dropped, while D2 shows the one-minute full scan is costly; D3 supports the targeted path but not its cold-start behavior.
uncertainty: Cold-start timing and stale interval are unmeasured.
minority: Frequent full scans offer a simpler freshness model if the 12-second cost is acceptable.

reviewConditions: Verify old source content is labeled stale until refresh completes
structured.revisit: Revisit the interval after the bounded timing and freshness trial.

result.summary: Conditional research proposal: test whether spaced recall improves handoff-to-completion transfer, without presuming an outcome.
alternatives: Controlled transfer experiment
Observational comparison of handoff quality and completion
risks: Vocabulary recall may not transfer to project completion; eight agents limit generalization.
result.nextAction: Researcher should preregister a bounded transfer experiment using handoff goals, revisions, unresolved questions, and a completion outcome, then compare against a non-spaced condition.

observations: Recall scores exist for 8 agents on vocabulary tasks; R1
Handoffs contain goals, revisions, and unresolved questions; R2
There is no established transfer-to-project-completion experiment; R3

questions: How might we test whether spaced recall changes a recipient's ability to carry a handoff through project completion, while preserving goals, revisions, and unresolved questions?
How might we compare a spaced-recall condition with a bounded control on completion of matched handoffs?
structured.challenge: Do not treat vocabulary recall scores as evidence of improved project outcomes; R1 and R3 require a direct transfer measure.

result.summary: Conditional research proposal: test spatial navigation as a retrieval aid, while using explicit relations—not distance—to identify conflicts.
alternatives: Navigation experiment with explicit-contradiction labels
Compare spatial and non-spatial retrieval interfaces
risks: Users may mistake proximity for evidence strength; nearby notes can be unrelated.
result.nextAction: Researcher should compare retrieval interfaces using the one explicit contradiction as ground truth and separately measure false conflict in the three nearby unrelated notes.
uncertainties: The effect of spatial layout on finding the explicit contradiction is unmeasured.

observations: Two graph layouts place linked claims nearby; R1
Proximity is navigation, not evidence strength; R2
One contradiction relation is explicit while three nearby notes have no relation; R3

questions: How might we test whether spatial proximity helps users retrieve explicitly conflicting claims without treating distance as evidence?
How might we measure retrieval of the explicit contradiction and false-conflict reports for the three nearby unrelated notes across spatial and non-spatial views?
structured.challenge: Reject any design that labels a conflict from distance alone; R2 and R3 require explicit relation grounding.

result.summary: Conditional risk proposal: make authorization and idempotency checks precede each separate write, with stable output identity.
alternatives: Authorize output creation then persist backlink with stable output ID
Transactional or resumable two-write workflow with reconciliation
risks: A crash between writes can leave a missing backlink or duplicate retry; revoked authority can change between checks.
result.nextAction: Workflow owner should define a dry-run two-write sequence that checks current delegate authority and stable output ID before each write, then inspect partial-write recovery without auto-approval.
uncertainties: Rollback guarantees and timing of authority revocation are unspecified.

structured.failureScenario: Assume the workshop appears complete but produces a duplicate output or a backlink after the delegate was revoked: the separate writes in K1 diverged, violating K2 or K3.

causes: Output and backlink writes can succeed independently; K1
Authority may be revoked before a later write; K2
Title-based retry matching can duplicate an output; K3

risks.value: A revoked delegate creates new output
Retry creates a duplicate when writes diverge

structured.reason: Prioritize authorization failure first because K2 is a hard safety constraint; stable IDs in K3 make duplicate detection a separate high-impact risk.

structured.mitigation: Re-check current authority before each write and reconcile by stable output ID; require explicit human review for partial states.
structured.earlySignal: A write is attempted with a revoked authority or an existing output ID has mismatched backlink state.

ownerAction.value: Draft and review the dry-run two-write recovery checklist; do not execute or auto-approve.

result.summary: Conditional economy proposal: treat fixed supply as an accounting invariant only, and separately review ownership, overdue escrow, and collusion risk.
alternatives: Escrow timeout and independent review checks
Supply ledger plus ownership-cluster review
risks: Conservation can hold while linked accounts collude or a subjective review remains unfairly overdue.
result.nextAction: Economy owner should inspect ownership relationships and overdue subjective reviews before any release, and verify supply conservation without treating it as fairness proof.
uncertainties: The true human ownership of three accounts and a fair overdue-review remedy are not established.

structured.failureScenario: Assume the pilot conserves all 5000 XP yet rewards a colluding account cluster or leaves a valid claim locked because subjective review is overdue.

causes: Three accounts may share one human owner; K2
Subjective review can be overdue while escrow remains locked; K3
Fixed supply constrains issuance but does not test collusion or fairness; K1

risks.value: Linked accounts distort participation or rewards
Escrow stays locked during overdue subjective review

structured.reason: Both can occur under conserved supply; prioritize ownership clustering for integrity, then overdue escrow for participant fairness.

structured.mitigation: Flag linked-account clusters for bounded human review and define an explicit overdue-review state before any escrow release; report conservation separately.
structured.earlySignal: Multiple accounts map to one owner or a subjective review crosses its deadline while escrow remains locked.

ownerAction.value: Record the two review triggers and refusal conditions; do not release XP or infer fairness.
